sections.content: How many people are "social and humanities scientists"?

9,065 people

were counted on the census as "social and humanities scientists" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Social and humanities scientists study and analyse human behaviour, the origin, structure and characteristics of language, undertake research in areas such as sociology, economics, politics, archaeology, history, philosophy, literature, and the arts, which may involve organising the collection of qualitative and quantitative data and analysing that information.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "social and humanities scientists" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "social and humanities scientists", 16.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "social and humanities scientists" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "social and humanities scientists" included:

  • civil engineers
  • newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters
  • musicians

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "social and humanities scientists" there were a similar number of men and women (47.2% compared with 52.8%).

This means "social and humanities scientists" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 47.2% and women made up 52.8% of "social and humanities scientists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "social and humanities scientists" included:

  • bakers and flour confectioners
  • laboratory technicians
  • packers, bottlers, canners and fillers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "social and humanities scientists" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "social and humanities scientists" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "social and humanities scientists", 14.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (75.5% compared with 24.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (78.3%) than self-employed (21.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wiltshire, this is in the region of the South West.
